overall: Temperatures surged to a running max of 84.2°F around 11:04 ET — well above NWP guidance — and have since turned decisively lower, now sitting at 82.4°F and falling at -1.8°F/hr (with an even sharper -3.1°F/hr over the last 30 minutes). Broken cloud cover (62%, BKN ceiling ~1311m) and a very moist airmass (dewpoint 73.4°F) characterized the day, which ran meaningfully hotter than models expected through midday before the cloud-driven cooling kicked in.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF 81.3°F, HRRR 82.1°F, NBM 81.0°F) clustered tightly in the 81–82°F range and were each beaten by 2–3°F by the observed running max of 84.2°F, indicating a systematic warm-side miss today — likely tied to the elevated overnight dewpoints and warm boundary layer that models underestimated. The NWP-forecast peak timing of ~11–12h ET did verify well even though the magnitude was off.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly already locked in at 84.2°F. With the peak confirmed at 11:04 ET, temperatures now declining at 1.8–3.1°F/hr, and persistent BKN cloud cover limiting solar insolation, a recovery above 84.2°F before sunset is very unlikely. The META model's top bucket is 84–85°F at 30.3%, consistent with the intraday model's 46.7% concentration in that same bucket, and the give-up classifier has not fired despite the running max already covering that range. Confidence is high that TMAX lands in the 84–85°F range, most probably near the already-observed 84.2°F floor.
